Ella Beatty arrives at the MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY premiere, just as her performance as Lizzie Borden starts becoming one of the biggest talking points around the new season.

She takes on one of America’s most infamous true crime figures and gives Lizzie a mix of vulnerability, rage, mystery and unpredictability that keeps you constantly questioning what she is really thinking.

What makes the performance work is how controlled it feels. Beatty can make Lizzie look completely innocent in one moment and genuinely unsettling in the next without ever pushing the character too far.

MONSTER may be built around the legend of Lizzie Borden, but Ella Beatty is the reason this version feels so difficult to look away from.

Fresh off its premiere at the Venice Film Festival, the gritty French courtroom thriller 'The Good Lawyer' (Un Bon Avocat) is officially coming to Netflix on November 9, 2026.

The film reunites 'Class Act' director Tristan Séguéla with leading man Laurent Lafitte, who plays a brilliant but addicted criminal defense lawyer. After collapsing in court and doing a stint in rehab, he has just one week to prepare for the trial of a lifetime involving a powerful industrial group and an international terrorist network.

An A-list French cast rounds out the production, including Anthony Bajon, Mélanie Laurent, and Carole Bouquet. Get all the details on the upcoming release:

‘A COUPLE OF LIES’ will be released on October 30, 2026, on Netflix, starring Frida Gustavsson and Fares Fares in a four-part Swedish psychological thriller. 

The series follows Helene and Carl, a couple hoping to escape their everyday lives by exchanging their home in Stockholm’s archipelago for a luxurious villa in Sicily. Their temporary escape comes through a house swap with Scarlett and Adam, another couple they have never met. What initially seems like the perfect opportunity for a relaxing getaway quickly begins to unravel. Unsettling discoveries inside their borrowed homes turn an ordinary vacation into something far more dangerous. 

As the two couples settle into each other’s lives, disturbing secrets begin emerging from places that should have remained private. The seemingly innocent arrangement gradually transforms into a dangerous game of surveillance, manipulation, and mistrust. Hidden betrayals threaten to destroy the relationships at the center of the story. Even the people closest to each other become impossible to trust. 

Frida Gustavsson portrays Helene, while Fares Fares plays her husband, Carl. Emma Appleton and Jakob Oftebro complete the central cast as Scarlett and Adam, the strangers who exchange homes with them. The story moves between the Swedish archipelago and the sun-drenched landscapes of Sicily, placing its psychological tension against two dramatically different settings. Behind the beautiful vacation homes lies a growing mystery about what each couple is keeping hidden. 

The limited series is based on the novel by bestselling Swedish crime author Stefan Ahnhem. Kasper Barfoed, who previously directed Netflix’s ‘THE NURSE,’ takes the helm of the adaptation. Amanda Högberg and Axel Stjärne adapted the story for television, bringing its tangled relationships and psychological manipulation to the screen. The four-episode format will contain the entire story within a single limited series. 

What makes ‘A COUPLE OF LIES’ particularly unsettling is how its central nightmare begins with something completely ordinary. Two couples agree to exchange their homes, only to discover that the arrangement exposes secrets within their own relationships. The story gradually replaces the promise of a perfect holiday with suspicion, betrayal, and the disturbing possibility that someone is watching. ‘A COUPLE OF LIES’ premieres October 30 on Netflix, bringing a twisted new psychological mystery to the streaming platform.

Ali Wong, Bette Midler, and Amanda Seyfried lead the star-studded cast of 'Steps', the upcoming animated feature from producer Amy Poehler. CARRIE officially arrives October 7, bringing Stephen King’s first novel back to the screen through Mike Flanagan’s eight episode reinvention. All eight episodes will release at once. 

Summer H. Howell stars as Carrie White, with Samantha Sloyan as Margaret White, Siena Agudong as Sue Snell, Alison Thornton as Chris Hargensen, Joel Oulette as Tommy Ross, Amber Midthunder as Miss Desjardin and Matthew Lillard as Principal Grayle. Howell reportedly beat out nearly 1,500 actors for the role. 

Flanagan is keeping the core tragedy of Carrie intact while moving the story firmly into the social media era, where bullying can spread far beyond a school hallway. The series will also expand Stephen King’s world with connections and references that were never explored in previous adaptations. 

The bullying, the telekinesis, the prom and all that blood are coming back. CARRIE premieres October 7, and Mike Flanagan finally gets his turn with one of Stephen King’s most devastating stories.

MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY is now officially streaming on Netflix, bringing Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s true crime anthology back for its fourth chapter. 

Ella Beatty stars as Lizzie Borden, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her father and stepmother in 1892 before later being acquitted at trial. 

Vicky Krieps stars as Bridget “Maggie” Sullivan alongside Charlie Hunnam as Andrew Borden, while Sarah Paulson appears as Aileen Wuornos as the story stretches across generations. 

The eight episode season makes Lizzie the first female subject of MONSTER, exploring repression, rage and the relationships surrounding one of America’s most infamous true crime mysteries. 

All eight episodes of MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY are now streaming on Netflix, and the anthology’s blood red era has officially begun.

The new season is available to stream now on Netflix, continuing the animated adventures set in the world of Stranger Things.

'A Couple of Lies' is the next Swedish psychological thriller to watch on Netflix. Starring Frida Gustavsson and Fares Fares, the 4-part series follows a house swap between two couples that quickly turns into a game of surveillance and mistrust.

The series is based on Stefan Ahnhem’s novel and is currently set to arrive on Netflix on October 30, 2026. Here is everything we know about the cast and plot.

Five years ago today, Squid Game premiered on Netflix and became a global phenomenon.

What initially arrived as a Korean survival thriller quickly grew into one of the most talked about shows of its era. Its deadly games, unforgettable characters, striking visuals, and sharp commentary on wealth and inequality helped the series connect with audiences far beyond South Korea.

Squid Game went on to become a major part of pop culture, inspiring countless discussions, costumes, references, and even real world experiences based on its iconic games. Five years later, its impact is still easy to recognize.

Imagine being the most famous actor in Japan, having a triumphant performance in London, and returning home only to realize nobody knows who you are. That's the premise of Netflix's upcoming Japanese comedy series, 'Did Someone Happen to Mention Me?'.

Starring Yakusho Koji alongside Alice in Borderland's Kaku Kento and Like a Dragon's Kawai Yuumi, the series explores a superstar's life after he hits rock bottom and must start entirely from scratch. 

'Did Someone Happen to Mention Me?' arrives on October 22, 2026. Here is everything we know so far about the cast, crew, and plot.

A beloved adaptation of Jane Austen’s ‘Pride and Prejudice’ is officially making its way to Netflix.

The classic six-part series is scheduled to arrive on the streaming platform on December 3, giving a new generation of viewers the opportunity to experience one of the most celebrated adaptations of Austen’s iconic novel.

First released in 1995, the miniseries follows Elizabeth Bennet as she navigates family expectations, social class, romance and the complicated relationship that develops between her and the wealthy, seemingly aloof Mr. Darcy.

What begins as mutual dislike gradually evolves into one of literature’s most enduring love stories, with Elizabeth and Darcy forced to confront their own assumptions about one another along the way.

The six-episode format also gives the adaptation considerably more room to explore Austen’s story than a traditional feature film. The Bennet family, their relationships, social circles and the pressures surrounding marriage all receive room to develop, helping create the richly detailed world that has made the series so memorable.

Its arrival on Netflix also comes at an interesting time, as Austen’s work continues to find new audiences through modern adaptations and reimaginings. With Netflix also preparing its own new ‘Pride and Prejudice’ series, viewers will soon have another opportunity to compare a fresh interpretation of the classic story with one of its most beloved adaptations.

For longtime fans, the December release is a chance to revisit a familiar favorite. For newcomers, it could be their first introduction to the version of Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy that has remained a fan favorite for decades.

The classic ‘Pride and Prejudice’ arrives on Netflix December 3.

Will you be revisiting this adaptation when it hits Netflix?

It's time. Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story is now streaming on Netflix. 

Trapped in a cruel Victorian-era household, Lizzie Borden kills her parents in a gory ax murder that shocks the nation.

MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY is officially streaming NOW, with all eight episodes finally available to watch.

Ella Beatty steps into the role of Lizzie Borden as the new season dives into the brutal 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, the explosive trial that followed and the mystery that has kept people debating Lizzie’s guilt for more than 130 years.

Sarah Paulson, Rebecca Hall, Vicky Krieps, Charlie Hunnam and Billie Lourd round out the stacked cast as the story explores the secrets, tensions and disturbing relationships inside the Borden household before everything turns deadly.

The countdown is over. The axe is out, the house is open, and MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY is finally here.

Charlie Hunnam is officially pulling double duty in the MONSTER universe, going from playing Ed Gein in Season 3 to portraying Andrew Borden in MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY. 

Hunnam completely transformed himself to play notorious murderer and grave robber Ed Gein, leading the third chapter of Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s true crime anthology. 

Now he steps into a completely different historical role as Andrew Borden, the wealthy father of Lizzie Borden whose brutal 1892 murder became one of America’s most infamous unsolved cases. 

Ella Beatty stars as Lizzie alongside Vicky Krieps, Rebecca Hall, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden and Sarah Paulson, with the new season taking the anthology into its blood red era. 

After becoming Ed Gein, Charlie Hunnam is jumping straight into another MONSTER story as MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY officially releases on Netflix tomorrow.

Eva Green has officially joined WEDNESDAY Season 3 as Aunt Ophelia, Morticia Addams’ mysterious missing sister and one of the biggest new characters heading into the next chapter. 

Ophelia was teased at the end of Season 2, where Wednesday discovers that her aunt is still alive and being kept inside Grandmama Hester’s mansion after years of questions surrounding her disappearance. 

Green is also reuniting with longtime collaborator Tim Burton after DARK SHADOWS, MISS PEREGRINE’S HOME FOR PECULIAR CHILDREN and DUMBO, with the showrunners describing her as the perfect fit for Ophelia’s elegant, haunting and unpredictable personality. 

Eva Green entering the Addams family as Aunt Ophelia honestly feels like casting that was waiting to happen.

THE DIPLOMAT Season 4 officially returns October 15 on Netflix, throwing Keri Russell’s Kate Wyler straight back into another political disaster with even more at stake than before.

The new season picks up after the explosive Season 3 finale, with the fragile peace between the United States and UK beginning to collapse while Kate’s already complicated marriage to Hal becomes even more dangerous.

Allison Janney and Bradley Whitford are back as Grace and Todd Penn, with Season 4 putting the two marriages at the center of the chaos as Grace and Hal’s secret alliance threatens to drag the United States toward war.

Political power, broken trust and two marriages barely holding together. THE DIPLOMAT is back October 15, and apparently nobody learned anything from last season.

WHY DID I GET MARRIED AGAIN? is officially the No. 1 movie on Netflix, debuting at the top of the streamer’s global English film chart with 19.3 million views. 

Tyler Perry’s third film reunites the original group for the destination wedding of Marcus and Angela’s daughter Jasmine, with Jill Scott, Tasha Smith, Michael Jai White, Richard T. Jones, Lamman Rucker and Sharon Leal returning alongside newcomer Taraji P. Henson. 

The movie arrived on Netflix on September 9 and immediately pushed THE WHISPER MAN down to No. 2, making the long awaited reunion the biggest English language movie on the platform this week. 

After bringing the couples back together years later, Tyler Perry apparently found the answer to “Why did we get married again?” Number one on Netflix.

Halloween has already begun on Netflix, ANNABELLE and THE CONJURING collections alongside both THE NUN movies now available to stream. 

The massive horror drop arrived on September 13, bringing together some of the biggest supernatural films from the shared CONJURING universe just in time for spooky season. 

The collection includes all three ANNABELLE movies, the first three main CONJURING films and both THE NUN chapters, giving viewers an entire marathon of possessions, haunted objects and demonic encounters.
 
Much of the franchise draws inspiration from the case files and paranormal claims associated with investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren, although the movies heavily fictionalize those stories for the screen.

Halloween may still be weeks away, but Netflix has already loaded up one of horror’s biggest universes for the perfect autumn nightmare marathon.

MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY officially releases on Netflix tomorrow, September 17, bringing Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan’s true crime anthology back for its fourth chapter. 

Ella Beatty stars as Lizzie Borden, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her father and stepmother with an axe in 1892 before later being acquitted at trial. 

The season also stars Vicky Krieps as Bridget “Maggie” Sullivan, Charlie Hunnam as Andrew Borden, Rebecca Hall as Abby Borden, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden and Sarah Paulson. 

The new chapter explores the cruelty, repression and relationships inside the Borden household while reimagining the events that turned Lizzie into one of the most infamous names in American true crime. 

MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY arrives tomorrow, and Netflix’s blood red MONSTER era is finally about to begin.

Netflix has officially canceled 'Ransom Canyon' after two seasons. Following a steep 43% viewership drop in Season 2, the Josh Duhamel and Minka Kelly drama won't be returning for Season 3.
